question: Before changing lanes, you should check your blind spots by

options.text: Looking into the rear view mirror.
Looking over your shoulder.
Looking at the side mirrors.

question: The 'two-second rule' is used in normal driving situation at

options.text: Certain speed only.
All speed.
Fixed speed only.

notes: Source grammar kept as printed: 'situation' (singular) and 'All speed.'

question: A new driver's licence will be revoked on accumulation of 13-demerit points

options.text: 12 months from the date of the grant of the licence.
18 months from the date of the grant of the licence.
24 months from the date of the grant of the licence.

notes: Source prints '13-demerit points' with a hyphen; kept as printed.

question: What must you do when a police vehicle with its siren on is behind you?

options.text: Continue to drive as normal.
Slow down and move to the side.
Speed up.

question: One of the reasons for you to have an accident with the vehicle you are following is that you

options.text: Follow too closely to the vehicle in front.
Follow the vehicle in front with too wide a gap.
Suddenly slow down and stop.

question: If you are in doubt of the depth of flood water (whether passable to vehicles), you should

options.text: Drive through slowly.
Drive through as quickly as possible.
Take an alternative route.

question: When driving an automatic car, you would select a lower gear

options.text: To control speed when going down a steep hill.
To slow the car down in normal driving.
Before stopping.

question: When entering an expressway, you should

options.text: Slow down to a speed suitable for joining the expressway.
Build up your speed to merge smoothly into the traffic stream.
Slow down and stop if necessary before joining the expressway.

question: When joining the expressway, you should

options.text: Always use the road shoulder.
Always give way to traffic already on the expressway.
Stop at the end of the acceleration lane.

question: Under what circumstances you may not follow the 'keep left rule'?

options.text: When travelling at the maximum speed limit of the road.
When traffic is light.
When your path is obstructed.

question: Using engine brake when travelling down slope would prevent

options.text: Over heating the brake linings.
Your tyres from wearing out too soon.
Damage to the brake system.

notes: Source prints 'Over heating' as two words; kept as printed.

question: We should use engine-brake when travelling downhill because

options.text: The brake linings will not over-heat and fade.
The engine is more durable than the brake linings.
The gears are more durable than the brake linings.

question: What is the correct footwork when changing from 2nd gear to 3rd gear?

options.text: Release the accelerator pedal and depress the clutch pedal at the same time.
Depress the accelerator and clutch together.
Depress the clutch pedal while keeping the accelerator on hold.

question: Pushing the clutch pedal down

options.text: Releases the engine from the wheels.
Engages the engine with the wheels.
Stalls the engine.

question: To maintain a steady speed while negotiating a mild bend, you should

options.text: Apply half-clutch.
Apply brake lightly.
Depress the accelerator pedal lightly.

question: When driving down a slope, you should use

options.text: A lower gear.
Higher gear.
The neutral gear.

question: When driving down a steep slope

options.text: Accelerate lightly to maintain a steady speed.
Change down to a lower gear to have better speed control.
Engage the neutral gear and use the brakes to control the speed.

question: When a motorcyclist tries to overtake you on the left, you should

options.text: Increase your speed to race the rider.
Reduce your speed and assist the rider to overtake safely.
Ignore the rider and continue driving at your normal speed.

question: When reversing, good observation is important. You should look

options.text: At the kerb and the side.
Ahead and at the side.
Through the rear windscreen, where your car is going.

question: When you are about to reverse, you should

options.text: Sound your horn to let others know that you are reversing your car.
Turn your head to look out for objects or persons at the rear of your car.
Look at the rear view mirror only.
